items.text: Connects WGS industry chain/business models with interactions among test quality, patents, and payment, generating policy knowledge rather than a clinical effectiveness trial.

The Policy Delphi is used to generate options, rationales, and disagreements rather than to force consensus; independent legal analysis, anonymous feedback, and minority opinions give the process epistemic value.
The continuously updated industry landscape, rankable issue list, alternatives for three tractable issues, and policy dissemination hold independent public-resource value.

Purposive expert selection, commercial interests, and attrition over five rounds can affect whose views enter the conclusions; patient/public-sector seats are present but do not constitute representative public opinion.

Score synthesis/tractability and screening into three predetermined domains may obscure important disagreements and marginal issues; the rationale and minority reasons must be disclosed, and consensus thresholds should not be treated as a necessary goal.

The original industry list and regulatory context are outdated; assessment at the current point in time requires updating specific policy issues. Dynamic monitoring exists, but the 20-month Delphi and three-year delivery still carry timeliness/access risks.
